transcript.content: Hi, it's nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, nice to meet you too. I guess what brings me in is… I feel like I’m always going from one thing to the next, like I can’t just sit in neutral, you know? And with the way work is set up now, it’s gotten harder to sort of cover that up.

I work customer service, so there’s always something going on anyway, calls, little issues, people needing answers—actually, some customers will tell you their whole life story before they get to the point—but lately it’s like the setup makes it more obvious that I’m constantly shifting around or needing to move on to something else. It’s not like a huge crisis, but it’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Have you had times when your mood felt unusually high or energized?

Um… unusually high? I’m not sure. I mean, I get energized sometimes, like if there’s a lot happening at work or I’ve had a good interaction with someone, but I don’t know if I’d call it “unusual.”

Sometimes I’ll get on a roll, like when the phones are nonstop and I’m bouncing between things, and then I come home and I’m still kind of keyed up. But that might just be the day, you know? I don’t think I’ve noticed anything like… way out of character, if that’s what you mean.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble sitting still?

Yeah, I think so. Looking back, it wasn’t just this recent work thing. Even in grade school, teachers would write stuff like I was bright but careless, or that I talked out of turn. I remember my mom getting those comments on report cards—well, I don’t remember every single one, but that kind of thing came up.

And they’d have to remind me to stay with my work. Sitting still was part of it, I guess, but it was more like I was always drifting off or jumping in before I was supposed to.
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep popping into your mind even when you try to ignore them?

I don’t think so… I mean, not in the way you’re saying, like thoughts that force their way in and I’m trying to push them out.

I’ll have stuff pop into my head, sure—like I’ll suddenly remember I meant to call someone back, or I’ll think about something random from work, and then that reminds me of another thing. Like the other day I was trying to watch TV and remembered a customer asking about a bill, and then I started thinking about whether I paid my own bill, and then somehow I was looking for the remote even though it was in my hand. But I don’t know if that’s what you mean by unwanted thoughts.

It’s more like my mind jumps around than like a scary or upsetting thought keeps coming back.
When you feel especially keyed up or energized, do you need less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure I’d say I need less sleep, no. If I’m keyed up after work, sometimes it takes me a while to wind down, like I’ll be thinking about calls or, you know, I’ll start doing some little thing around the house and then notice it’s later than I meant.

But I don’t think I’ve had that thing where I’m sleeping way less and still feel totally fine. At least, I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I don’t know if I’d call it worrying a lot for no reason. I mean, I worry about normal stuff—bills, work things, whether I forgot to do something. Sometimes I’ll get stuck thinking about, you know, did I send that email or did I leave something undone, and then I end up checking something else, like the mail or the calendar, and then I’m off on that.

But it’s usually tied to something, I think. Not just sitting there anxious out of nowhere. At least not that I’ve really noticed.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on one task from start to finish?

Yeah, that happens. Like, I’ll start out okay, especially if it’s something at work, but if it’s one of those longer coaching meetings or I’m reading a new procedure, after a few minutes I’ll realize my eyes were moving across the page or I was looking at the person talking, but I didn’t really take in what they said.

Then I kind of have to back up and figure out where I lost it. Sometimes I’ll think I’m following, and then they mention some detail and I’m like, wait, when did we get to that part? It’s not that I’m trying not to pay attention… it just slips.
Do you spend much of the day feeling worried or on edge?

I wouldn’t say much of the day, no. I mean, I get tense if there’s something hanging over me, like if I think I forgot a customer follow-up or I’ve got a bunch of little things stacked up. That can kind of sit in the back of my mind.

But “on edge” all day… I don’t know. Not really. Sometimes I’m just busy or distracted, and then I’ll remember something I meant to do—actually, that happened yesterday with the trash bins, I walked right past them twice—but that’s more aggravating than worried, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with childhood onset and persistent current symptoms of inattention and hyperactive/impulsive traits. The patient confirms longstanding distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention, careless mistakes, talking out of turn, trouble staying with work, and being constantly on the go.
